statement: Reference validator path rules are POSIX-only on a Windows-native target: NTFS alternate data streams, reserved device names, trailing dot/space aliases are accepted; no junction/reparse-point check; contradicts Security §8.2 claim that the validator implements step 2 and T-PARSE-04
evidence: negctl P09 (data/notes.txt:hidden), P10 (data/CON.txt), P11 (data/documents.jsonl.) ACCEPTED; bundle.py _safe_rel and common.schema relative_path; only is_symlink() checked
requested_action: Reject ':' , reserved names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9 with any extension), trailing '.' or ' ', case-insensitive duplicate paths, junctions (Path.is_junction) and over-long paths in both _safe_rel and the relative_path schema; add tests

statement: Signature trust is weaker than documented: validator silently accepts a dev- prefixed key_id when that key is pinned (Security §8.1 and T-UPD-01 say dev- ids are refused in production); after a signature failure it continues to parse untrusted records (not fail-fast versus the directive sequence); who may change the pinned trust list is unspecified, so a site Admin could add a key and bypass owner custody
evidence: bundle.py verify_signature declared.removeprefix('dev-'); negctl N20 accepted with no warning; P12 records_parsed=4 after SIGNATURE_INVALID; SECURITY §8.1 'site Admin removes the old key from the trust list'
requested_action: Add a production mode that rejects dev- ids (and warns in dev mode); stop after any step-1/step-2 error before parsing records; specify that the trust list is changed only by an installer/OS-administrator action with owner fingerprint confirmation and an audit event; add tests

statement: Withdrawal and restriction do not propagate across time: the retained N-1 generation and rollback can resurrect withdrawn or newly restricted items; no channel or procedure delivers a register update (RM-002) or purges existing generations, derivatives, embeddings and backups; Admin uploads of restricted bytes are 'quarantined' and so retained and backed up, conflicting with the register's routine_operations_forbidden: copy
evidence: SECURITY §8.2 step 7 'keep N-1', §8.3 backups, T-RM-02 'Quarantined'; register RM-001 routine_operations_forbidden [copy, redistribute, delete]; no text on rollback vs withdrawal
requested_action: Define: withdrawal and register changes apply to every retained generation and block rollback to a generation containing excluded items; signed register-update channel; purge procedure for derivatives/indexes/backups; restricted uploads rejected with hash-only record (owner decision if retention is needed); add T-VIS/T-RM tests for rollback

statement: Client-side persistence on shared office desktops is not covered: recent queries 'local to the user', persisted tabs, 'read-only cached view of open tabs' when offline; no Cache-Control: no-store for originals/snippets, no purge on logout; T-VIS-02 omits browser caches (withdrawn content and incident queries can persist)
evidence: design 03 §2 suggestions, §5 tabs persist; 06 §2.4 Server unreachable cached view; P-CDR uses shared desktop; SECURITY §9.2 T-VIS-02 lists FTS/vector/graph/caches/exports only
requested_action: Specify server-side storage for per-user state, Cache-Control: no-store/private for document and API responses, logout purge (Clear-Site-Data), no service worker/offline cache of document content; add a browser-cache leak test

statement: The directive's nine-layer data separation (vault, derivatives, provenance, candidates, reviewed, authenticated, publication state, indexes, working docs) is not specified as a whole; reviewed records, authentication/approval records and publication-state history have no schema or storage model; review_ref/approval_ref are unverifiable free strings; publication is a producer-set field in the bundle although ADR-0002 makes publication a site Admin act
